title: Test Your Understanding: Fan-Out on Write vs Read
description: Push vs pull timelines, celebrity problem, and hybrid feeds.

questions.question: Fan-out on write (push model) precomputes timelines by:

options.text: Querying all followees' posts when the user opens the app
Inserting the new post into each follower's inbox when someone posts
Caching only the celebrity user's outbox
Deleting old posts from follower inboxes

questions.explanation: Push model writes to follower inboxes at post time. Reads fetch prebuilt inbox — fast scroll, expensive writes for high follower counts.

questions.question: The main risk of pure fan-out on write is:

options.text: Slow reads for users with few followers
Write amplification when a user with millions of followers posts
Inability to store posts
Push requires WebSockets

questions.explanation: Each post from a celebrity triggers millions of inbox writes — the hot-user/celebrity problem.

questions.question: A common hybrid feed strategy is:

options.text: Push for all users including celebrities
Pull for everyone with no inbox
Push for normal users; pull celebrity posts at read time
Never use queues for fan-out

questions.explanation: Threshold on follower count: push below K, store hot users' posts in outbox only and merge on read.

questions.question: Fan-out on read makes writes cheap but:

options.text: Read must merge posts from many followees
Cannot support pagination
Requires one global inbox table
Eliminates need for caching

questions.explanation: Read path queries/merges multiple outboxes — cost scales with follow count unless cached or limited.

questions.question: Async fan-out workers should use idempotency because:

options.text: Queues guarantee exactly-once delivery
At-least-once delivery can duplicate inbox inserts
Posts cannot be deleted
Followers never change

questions.explanation: Retry/redelivery of fan-out jobs must not duplicate (follower_id, post_id) rows.

questions.question: Redis sorted sets (score = timestamp) are a reasonable inbox storage pattern for timelines.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: ZSET gives time-ordered post IDs per user — common pattern for push inboxes with pagination by score.

questions.question: Which help with the celebrity problem? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Follower-count threshold for push vs pull
Synchronous fan-out in the post HTTP handler
Push only to recently active followers
Ignoring follower distribution in load tests

questions.explanation: Hybrid thresholds and active-only push reduce write blast radius. Sync fan-out and unrealistic test data hide the problem.

questions.question: For a v1 interview feed design, chronological merge without ML ranking means:

options.text: You cannot use push or pull
Sort merged posts by timestamp; ranking is a later layer
CAP theorem does not apply
You must shard by post_id only

questions.explanation: Start with time-ordered timeline; algorithmic ranking adds candidate scoring on top of push/pull mechanics.
